correctness.rationale: The exact integral formal-series identity \(S(z)^2=S(z)-z+2T(z)\) implies \(F(z)=(S(z)/z)/(1-2T(z)/z)\); modulo \(2^N\), only terms with \(r<N\) occur. Any nonzero term forces \(n+r+1\) to be a sum of \(2r+1\) powers of two, hence \(s_2(n+r+1)\le2r+1\). Subadditivity with \(N-r-1\) gives \(s_2(n+N)\le2N-1\). Translation by \(N\) proves the stated binomial-coefficient upper bound. The independent recurrence and factorized-series calculations agree for 2048 coefficients and test 4,718,592 index/precision cases. No unproved analytic or computational lemma is required.

value.rationale: The binary-composition function has a documented modulo-prime-power sparsity phenomenon. The new formula reduces the sufficient binary-weight cutoff from exponential \(2^N\) to linear \(2N\), and yields the explicit all-precision exceptional-count upper bound \(O_N((\log x)^{2N-1})\). This substantially quantifies a motivated arithmetic-divisibility question and rests on a structural formal-series identity, rather than on finite numerical enumeration.
